title: Adaptations or full originals
statement: Should a course teach a classic work through short adaptations, through the full original with companion sessions, or through a reviewed mix of the two?
detail: A source audit of a Grade 3 reading course found its lesson designs explicitly teaching short supplied adaptations, while a newly supplied sourcing portal asks for complete originals and prohibits replacing the original with a retelling (`grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-08/all-grades-source-audit/GRADE3.md`, lines 13 and 89). Replacing the readings alone would invalidate many exact-evidence questions, vocabulary bindings, models and narration, so the audit asks for a named academic decision between adaptations, full originals with companion sessions, or a reviewed combination, and makes none of the changes itself (same file, line 89). A card from the same sourcing portal makes a named retelling the intended core reading for another grade, so a blanket conclusion that a retelling can only be scaffolding was withdrawn (`grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-08/all-grades-source-audit/GRADE4.md`, line 74).

evidence.quote: This conflicts with the existing lesson designs, which explicitly teach short supplied adaptations.
Replacing readings alone would invalidate many current exact-evidence questions, vocabulary bindings, models and narration.
A named academic decision must establish whether the course uses adaptations, full originals with companion sessions, or a reviewed combination.
This card establishes a named retelling as an intended **core**, so any blanket conclusion that a retelling can only be scaffolding is withdrawn.
